The reference unit defines this independently configurable seconds interval, while the connection unit defines the ordinary elapsed-time gate.

Either internal check ordering therefore permits this timing. The approved reference unit permits independent secret refresh without a sentinel change. This answer is appropriate when the first listed secret-due invocation demonstrably clears both gates, as here; it is not a guarantee for closer-spaced calls, unbounded prior work or a fixed-version reference. C incorrectly imposes the watched ordinary-setting reload condition on the independent secret path. A changed watched sentinel is a genuine correct condition for the ordinary-setting publication/reload pattern, together with an eligible explicit call, but it is not necessary for this versionless secret's interval-based refresh. No event-driven push or automatic scheduling is inferred from either path.
